description: The bar chart illustrates classification accuracy (%) on novel real-world tasks across six different model configurations, as evaluated in the paper “LaSQuE: Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning.” The vertical y-axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 40% to 65% in increments of 5%, while the horizontal x-axis lists the six models without explicit category labels, ordered from left to right as: RoBERTa w/o Exp., ExEnt, LaSQuE (mean), LaSQuE, LaSQuE (syn2real), and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum). The legend on the right identifies each model with a distinct color: light gray for RoBERTa w/o Exp. (~46%), light blue for ExEnt (~55%), orange for LaSQuE (mean) (~47%), green for LaSQuE (~47%), purple for LaSQuE (syn2real) (~59%), and dark gray for LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) (~62%). The bars are sorted in increasing order of performance, with the final model achieving the highest accuracy. No error bars or statistical annotations are visible, and all bars are solid-colored with no patterns or shading. The chart visually emphasizes the performance gains from incorporating synthetic-to-real adaptation and curriculum learning into the LaSQuE framework.
